properties.statement:
REFLOW2'S OWN COMMAND SURFACE EXISTS IN FIVE PLACES AND NOTHING CHECKS THAT THEY AGREE. Measured 2026-09-01, prompted by Anthony asking why a count was 23.

  getting-started/skills/     25  SOURCE — compiled into the binary
  .claude/skills/            25  copy, for harness auto-matching
  .grok/skills/              25  copy
  getting-started/commands/  28  SOURCE for the slash commands
  .claude/commands/          28  copy
  ~/.claude/commands/        24  USER SCOPE — what every OTHER project sees
  COMMAND_ALIASES            8   the skill<->command name map, in skills.rs

WHAT WAS ALREADY IN STEP, checked rather than assumed: the three skill directories are byte-identical, and `getting-started/commands/` matches `.claude/commands/` exactly. The drift is not everywhere.

🛑 WHERE IT HAD DRIFTED, both found by measuring rather than reported:
① FOUR COMMANDS EXISTED ONLY IN THIS REPO — `/link-ideas`, `/root-cause`, `/what-is-this`, `/where-does-it-go`. User scope is what every other project on this machine sees, so in bhome, musicjug and ophyd-service those four did not exist. `/root-cause` is the sharpest loss: its whole argument is that it must be pulled AT THE MOMENT of the work, and it is missing from exactly the projects where work happens. (Copied across the same day; nothing prevents recurrence.)
② THE ALIAS TABLE IS MISSING THREE OF ELEVEN. It carries `rules`, `req`, `gaps`, `where`, `kpp`, `health`, `decisions`, `debt` — and NOT `what-is-this` -> `help`, `where-does-it-go` -> `onboarding`, or `next` (tool-backed). So `get_skill("what-is-this")` fails with a bare list of names, which is the precise failure reported on 2026-08-19 that caused the table to be written. The repair did not cover its own class.

⭐ THE TWO HALVES HAVE OPPOSITE GUARANTEES, AND THAT IS THE CAUSE WORTH NAMING. Skills are SERVED from the binary (`dec:skills-served`) specifically so they cannot drift from the running version. Slash commands are COPIED FILES, so they can and did. One surface was designed against this failure and the other was not — and the copied half is the one a user in another project actually meets.

📌 AND AN AGENT WITH FULL ACCESS UNDER-REPORTED IT BY 60%. Asked what commands exist, this session listed 11 of 28 — having matched command names against skill names and reported the 17 aliased ones as reachable only through `get_skill`. Anthony caught it. That is the same shape musicjug reported the day before ("reflow2 ships find_tools and I never used it because nothing told me how it differs"), arriving this time from the inside: the surface is not discoverable even to something reading the directory.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether user-scope drift has ever cost anybody anything. Nobody has reported reaching for one of the four and finding it absent — the loss is inferred from what the commands are for, not observed.

═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01, AND DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

WHAT MOVED: "nothing checks that they agree" is no longer true of the surfaces INSIDE the repository. `tools/check_command_surface.py` runs in CI and compares the three skill directories, the command source against its copy, every skill against a command that reaches it, every command against a skill that exists, and every renamed command against the alias table. `COMMAND_ALIASES` is complete, and `list_skills` now states each skill's `shortcut` so nobody has to derive the mapping. ① and ② above are both repaired (`chg:the-command-surface-answers-for-itself`).

🛑 WHAT STILL STANDS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT CLOSED: **user scope remains unreachable.** `~/.claude/commands/` lives outside the repository, so CI cannot see it; the check reports it as a NOTE and never a failure, on the machine that happens to run it and no other. The four-command gap that started this can recur on any machine with the build staying green. Closing this fact would assert a completeness the repair does not have.

⭐ AND THE SAME BLIND SPOT CAUGHT THE AGENT AGAIN, an hour later, which is why it is recorded here rather than as its own node. Told that the ophyd-service work had been done on a work laptop, this session stated as fact that the laptop was "behind" and missing the four commands. It could not see that machine. Anthony challenged it and the claim collapsed to an inference — plausible, because user-scope copies are per-machine and nothing syncs them, but not observed. **Second time in one day that this session asserted something about a surface it could not measure, both about the same surface.** The honest form is the one the check itself takes: report the note, name what it could not look at, and do not upgrade an inference into an observation.
